findings.title: Use a real installer source or remove this build step
findings.whyItBreaks: https://example.com/install.sh currently returns HTTP 404 with HTML. Because curl neither uses --fail nor validates content, that HTML is piped to sh, causing the image build to fail.

findings.title: Pin and verify the downloaded installer before executing it
findings.whyItBreaks: The build executes whatever bytes the remote URL serves as root, without a version pin, checksum, signature, or trusted package source. A compromised or changed endpoint can inject arbitrary code into builds and resulting images.

findings.title: Preserve missing-key status in the exported helper
findings.whyItBreaks: Load returns ErrMissing for an absent key, while a present key may validly contain "". Discarding that error makes both cases return "" to every caller of this exported API, so callers cannot safely distinguish missing data from a real empty value.

findings.title: Wait for result sends before returning
findings.whyItBreaks: Each send now runs in an untracked goroutine, so Run can return before any result is delivered. A caller that treats return as completion and closes results can cause these goroutines to panic with "send on closed channel"; a receiver that closes/continues based on Run returning can also miss results.

findings.title: Require both admin status and tenant match
findings.whyItBreaks: Replacing && with || allows a non-admin whose tenant matches the record to delete it, and allows an admin from a different tenant to delete it. The previous predicate required both authorization conditions.

findings.title: Implement the clamping promised by clampPercent
findings.whyItBreaks: `clampPercent` returns unbounded values: for example, `clampPercent(150, 100)` returns 150 and `clampPercent(-1, 100)` returns -1. The exported name promises a bounded percent, and the latter value also makes `progressBar` call `String#repeat` with a negative count.

findings.title: Preserve parse failures when updating settings
findings.whyItBreaks: A malformed or incomplete settings value now becomes DEFAULTS. updateFontSize then changes its font size and calls save, whereas before parseSettings threw before save. For example, '{"theme":"dark"}' with size 16 is saved as '{"theme":"light","fontSize":16}', silently discarding the existing theme.

findings.title: Count the final partial page
findings.whyItBreaks: For totals not evenly divisible by pageSize, Math.floor undercounts pages: pageCount(11, 10) returns 1 although items 1-10 and 11 require two pages. Consumers will not expose the final partial page.

facts.meaning: The page count rounds down instead of up.
A remainder/partial final page is omitted or a small result becomes zero pages.

findings.title: Fetch artifacts for the requested branch's commit
findings.whyItBreaks: For a requested branch whose ref differs from "verified", the report says builtFrom is the requested commit but returns artifacts belonging to the verified commit. Consumers receive a self-inconsistent report and can publish or display artifacts for the wrong build.

findings.title: Restore the limit when returning sorted entries
findings.whyItBreaks: The public contract promises at most limit entries, but this returns every entry whenever limit is positive. renderFeed calls it with 20 at src/feed.ts:9, so feeds with more than 20 items now exceed the intended page size.

findings.title: End the month range at the next month's start
findings.whyItBreaks: For month=10, this produces an end of 2026-10-31T00:00:00. The half-open predicate at src/lib/date-range.ts:32 requires issuedAt < end, so the monthly filter at src/reports/monthly.ts:17 excludes every non-void invoice issued on October 31. monthlyCsv then serializes that undercount via src/reports/export.ts:5.

facts.meaning: monthRange's end is now day 0 of the following month (the requested month's last day at midnight) instead of the first day of the next month.
Records on the last day of a month fall outside the half-open range and are omitted from monthly totals.

findings.title: Count only rendered entries in the manifest header
findings.whyItBreaks: After stale entries are removed, the body emits one row per `live` entry but the header still receives `entries.length`. A manifest with one live and one stale entry therefore declares `# entry-count: 2` while containing one entry, breaking consumers that use the header to validate or preallocate for the listed rows.

findings.title: Restore the exported legacy formatter
findings.whyItBreaks: Removing FormatLegacyID breaks compilation for any consumer of example.com/app/ids that still formats persisted or interoperable LEG-prefixed identifiers.

findings.title: Preserve the exported shippingQuote API
findings.whyItBreaks: Replacing the exported shippingQuote function with an imported quoteShipping implementation removes the shippingQuote export from this module. Existing consumers importing { shippingQuote } from src/orders will fail to compile after upgrading.

findings.title: Return the transformed input instead of always throwing
findings.whyItBreaks: Every invocation of execute now throws "always fails"; callers can no longer receive the string promised by its string return type. The prior behavior returned input.toUpperCase().

findings.title: Preserve the viewer read-only path
findings.whyItBreaks: An active viewer below the attempt limit previously passed isEligible and handle returned "read-only" at line 25. This new rejection returns "rejected" at line 24 instead, making the explicitly supported viewer behavior unreachable.

findings.title: Keep draft saves independent of payment
findings.whyItBreaks: For `{ state: "draft", payment: "missing" }`, the new condition returns false and `saveDraft` returns "blocked". An unpaid order must be saveable as a draft; payment governs submitting an order, not persisting unfinished work.

findings.title: Read files from the snapshot commit
findings.whyItBreaks: For any channel other than "stable", the returned Snapshot declares commit=headCommit(channel) but contains filesAt(headCommit("stable")). Consumers reading a snapshot will therefore see file contents that do not belong to its advertised commit.

findings.title: Honor the limit parameter
findings.whyItBreaks: `limit` promises a caller-controlled output cap, but the function still assigns `max_count = 10`; for example, `build("x", 3)` returns 10 entries instead of 3.

findings.title: Enforce positivity in parse_positive_int
findings.whyItBreaks: parse_positive_int(-1) returns -1 despite its public name promising a positive value. charge then turns it into -100 cents, so callers receive an invalid negative charge rather than a validation failure.

findings.title: Preserve the caller's DataFrame
findings.whyItBreaks: The prior implementation copied df and modified only that copy. The new implementation writes through df.loc and returns the same object, so a caller that keeps df as an unmodified baseline will find its "value" cells changed after calling apply_values.

findings.title: Restore the CI workflow under .github/workflows
findings.whyItBreaks: GitHub Actions only discovers workflow YAML files in .github/workflows. This rename removes ci.yml from that directory and leaves identical YAML under docs/, where it is documentation rather than an executable workflow. Pushes and pull requests will no longer run npm ci, lint, or tests.

findings.title: Enforce positivity or retain the generic parser name
findings.whyItBreaks: `parse_positive_int("-5")` returns `-5`, contrary to its public name; `charge("-5")` consequently returns `-500`. Public callers may rely on the renamed contract to skip their own positivity validation.

findings.title: Avoid moving items before reading its length
findings.whyItBreaks: `dbg!(items)` takes ownership of the Vec and its returned value is discarded by the semicolon. `items.len()` on line 3 then borrows a moved value, causing Rust error E0382.

findings.title: Compute changed paths from the emitted base revision
findings.whyItBreaks: The returned Changeset declares fromRevision as the resolved pinned tag, but changedPaths is now calculated relative to the separately resolved latest tag. When the tags differ, consumers replay paths derived from latest on top of the pinned revision, violating the documented pairing and producing an incorrect changeset.

findings.title: Update the query for the renamed email column
findings.whyItBreaks: After this migration, users.email no longer exists, but src/query.sql still executes SELECT email FROM users. Any execution after migration fails with a missing-column SQL error.

findings.title: Remove the hardcoded live billing API key
findings.whyItBreaks: The bk_live credential is committed to the repository, exposing it to every repository reader and forcing all deployments to use the same production secret rather than their configured environment credential.

findings.title: Allow administrators to purge archived projects
findings.whyItBreaks: For user.isAdmin=true and project.archived=true, the new first guard returns "forbidden" before db.delete runs. The base implementation purged that same project, so the administrative purge workflow is now blocked.

facts.meaning: The refactored guard incorrectly returns forbidden for administrators.
Non-administrators can reach the destructive project purge/delete path.
The refactored guard incorrectly returns forbidden for administrators.

findings.title: Restore handling for missing settings files
findings.whyItBreaks: load_settings() returns None when path does not exist, but startup() now immediately subscripts that value. A previously supported missing-config startup path therefore raises TypeError instead of starting with one worker.

findings.title: Propagate gateway submission failures
findings.whyItBreaks: When Gateway.Submit returns an error, Charge only logs it and returns nil. As an exported payment API, this forces every caller to treat a declined or failed charge as successful and may cause orders to be fulfilled without payment.

findings.title: Include tenant ID in the settings cache key
findings.whyItBreaks: settingsFor("tenant-a", "theme", ...) caches under settings:theme; a later settingsFor("tenant-b", "theme", ...) returns tenant-a's cached value without calling store.fetch. Tenant-specific settings are therefore misrouted across tenants.

findings.title: Preserve the exported invalidate call signature
findings.whyItBreaks: Existing JavaScript callers using invalidate(tenantId, name) now pass tenantId as the sole name argument, so they delete settings:<tenantId> rather than the cached setting. TypeScript callers fail recompilation because the exported function no longer accepts two arguments.

findings.title: Serialize reservations across the persistence await
findings.whyItBreaks: With stock loaded as 1, two concurrent calls both read remaining=1 before either await completes. Both save 0, both set local stock to 0, and both resolve true, so two reservations are accepted for one item.

findings.title: Update retry to consume millisecond backoff values
findings.whyItBreaks: backoff(0) now returns 1,000 milliseconds, but retry still multiplies it by 1,000 before passing it to sleep. The first retry therefore waits 1,000,000 ms (16m40s) instead of 1 second; later retries are likewise inflated by 1,000x.

findings.title: Propagate the file close error
findings.whyItBreaks: The deferred Close result is discarded. Previously, a successful Flush followed by a failing Close returned that failure from Save (base store/save.go:25); now Save returns nil from Flush and callers cannot distinguish a completed save from a close failure.

findings.title: Include the final row in each page window
findings.whyItBreaks: _window_bounds returns half-open bounds, but range(start, end - 1) excludes the final valid row. Every full page loses one row; a page_size of 1 produces an empty page. render_page and summarize consume this result, so their output omits data.

findings.title: Restore the TTL validity comparison
findings.whyItBreaks: A freshly stored entry has age 0, which fails `0 > ttlMs`, so it is deleted and returned as a cache miss. Entries older than the TTL instead remain readable indefinitely.

findings.title: Do not splice jobs while iterating with forEach
findings.whyItBreaks: Removing an item shifts the next item into its index while `forEach` advances to the next index. For `[done, done]`, the second completed job is skipped and returned instead of being pruned.

findings.title: Preserve the zero result for empty row sets
findings.whyItBreaks: For rows=[], reduce returns 0 and division by rows.length returns NaN; the prior implementation returned 0 for this public function's empty-input case.

findings.title: Do not reorder the caller's rows array
findings.whyItBreaks: Array.prototype.sort mutates rows in place. Previously busiest sorted a copied array, so callers could retain their original ordering after asking for the busiest row.

findings.title: Sort ranking scores numerically
findings.whyItBreaks: Array.prototype.sort() orders numbers as strings. For scores [9, 100, 99] and n=2, the reversed ranking becomes [99, 9, 100], setting cutoff to 9; topPlayers then returns 9 and 100 from that input order, incorrectly excluding 99.

findings.title: Restore constant-time signature comparison
findings.whyItBreaks: Plain string equality exits at the first mismatched character, exposing comparison timing that can let a remote caller progressively infer a valid HMAC and forge an authenticated webhook request. The prior hmac.compare_digest call avoided this side channel.

findings.title: Keep ledger and balance updates in one transaction
findings.whyItBreaks: The transaction exits and commits immediately after `_record_ledger`. If either balance UPDATE then fails, the ledger records a completed transfer while one or both account balances were not updated; if the second UPDATE fails, the source may also be debited without crediting the destination.

findings.title: Preserve UTC when deriving billing days
findings.whyItBreaks: The previous implementation explicitly derived all components in UTC. The new local-time getters make the result depend on the server timezone: for example, under America/Los_Angeles, 2026-01-01T00:30:00Z now produces 2025-12-31 instead of 2026-01-01, causing transactions to be assigned to the wrong billing day.

findings.title: Restore tenant scoping in the profile cache key
findings.whyItBreaks: The module-level memo now uses only account as its key. After tenant A reads account X, a read for tenant B/account X returns tenant A's cached Profile without calling fetchProfile, exposing incorrect cross-tenant data.

findings.title: Preserve missing-key errors from load
findings.whyItBreaks: A missing key now returns "", which is also a valid stored string. loadAll therefore silently returns partial data containing empty strings where it previously threw, so callers cannot distinguish absent data from an intentional empty value.

findings.title: Preserve the existing Config shape for retry callers
findings.whyItBreaks: Existing consumers of exported retry that pass { maxAttempts, timeoutMs } no longer type-check: timeoutMs was removed and an unrelated required retries property was added.

findings.title: Make retryBackground non-blocking or rename it
findings.whyItBreaks: The exported name promises background execution, but it immediately invokes fn() synchronously and can block the caller for every retry attempt. Its implementation duplicates the synchronous retry behavior.

findings.title: Expose exhausted retry failures from retryBackground
findings.whyItBreaks: Every exception is discarded and both success and exhausted retries return undefined. Public callers therefore cannot distinguish a completed operation from a failed one.

findings.title: Handle numeric Field values before reading length
findings.whyItBreaks: `FieldProps` now promises callers may pass a number, but `value.length` is undefined for numbers. Rendering `<Field value={42} />` consequently produces `len=undefined` instead of the numeric string length; TypeScript also rejects the property access on `string | number`.

findings.title: Retain a buffer large enough for PR diffs
findings.whyItBreaks: Removing maxBuffer restores spawnSync's 1 MiB default. A valid PR whose git diff exceeds that limit makes the git diff call at line 140 terminate with ENOBUFS; git() then throws and the review job reports failure instead of reviewing the PR. The previous 64 MiB bound explicitly supported these diffs.

findings.title: Restore the read-only sandbox for review runs
findings.whyItBreaks: Removing `-s read-only` causes the subprocess receiving `prompt` to run with Codex's default sandbox rather than the prior enforced read-only mode. Because its working directory is `opts.repoPath`, a prompt can now direct the review agent to overwrite or delete files in the repository under review.

findings.title: Diff from the merge base before reviewing the PR
findings.whyItBreaks: When PR_BASE_SHA is a newer base-branch commit than the PR's fork point, it is not an ancestor of the PR head. `git diff baseSha HEAD` then includes base-branch-only changes as reversions, so the review bundle and changed-file set contain unrelated files and omit the actual PR-only range.

findings.title: Preserve literal prompt payloads during replacement
findings.whyItBreaks: String.prototype.replace interprets $&, $`, $', and $$ in a string replacement. bundle.patch is repository-controlled text and is inserted both through JSON.stringify(bundle) and directly into {{PATCH}}; a patch containing $& will insert the placeholder match itself, while $`/$' inject surrounding prompt text. The previous callback replacements preserved these values literally, so affected review/critic prompts are now malformed.

findings.title: Pin fallback reviews to the analyzed SHA
findings.whyItBreaks: If the initial review request fails and the PR receives a new commit before this fallback runs, omitting commit_id makes GitHub associate the fallback REQUEST_CHANGES or approval with the PR's then-current latest commit, rather than headSha that Needlefish analyzed. This can block or approve code that was not reviewed.

findings.title: Reject malformed findings instead of inventing P1 results
findings.whyItBreaks: A structurally valid review containing `findings: [{}]` now returns a purported finding with severity `P1`, category `bug`, an empty file, and line 0. Previously the invalid severity, required text fields, file, and line numbers caused normalization to throw. Consumers can no longer distinguish malformed review output from a real high-priority finding.

findings.title: Retain an explicit repository for manual PR ref resolution
findings.whyItBreaks: On workflow_dispatch, EVENT_HEAD is empty and this runs before actions/checkout, so the workspace has no Git remote from which gh can infer a repository. gh pr view therefore cannot resolve PR_NUM; command substitution writes empty head/base outputs, and the following checkout does not check out the requested PR head.

findings.title: Reject incomplete review payloads
findings.whyItBreaks: Missing required fields now become empty strings or arrays. For example, {"summary":"ok"} produces a RawReview with no findings, checked evidence, or residual risks, which is indistinguishable from a valid clean review; previously this payload threw an explicit malformed-output error.

findings.title: Restore PR-ref resolution for manual dispatch
findings.whyItBreaks: For workflow_dispatch, github.event.pull_request is absent. The checkout expression therefore selects github.ref rather than the supplied PR’s head, the base fetch defaults to main rather than the PR’s target branch, and both PR_BASE_SHA and PR_HEAD_SHA are empty. A manually requested review can consequently execute the workflow-ref version of Needlefish and compare/review the wrong revision instead of the requested PR.

findings.title: Restore a large output buffer for git diff
findings.whyItBreaks: spawnSync defaults maxBuffer to 1 MiB when omitted. The changed helper is used to collect the full base-to-HEAD diff at line 100; any larger diff now terminates with a buffer error and prevents the local review from running, whereas the prior 64 MiB limit supported it.

findings.title: Keep review errors failing the check
findings.whyItBreaks: When review() throws, this path still says the PR did not pass and exits nonzero, but it publishes a neutral Check Run conclusion. GitHub treats neutral as successful for required status checks, so a required Needlefish check can allow merging after the review failed to run.

findings.title: Restore the tool checkout before installing dependencies
findings.whyItBreaks: The repository head contains only .github/workflows/review.yml and .needlefish/answers.json; it has no package.json. Consequently `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` runs in the repository root and fails before the review can execute.

findings.title: Do not execute the PR checkout as the privileged reviewer
findings.whyItBreaks: A same-repository PR can modify src/cli.ts (and its dependency manifest) and this step executes it after exposing GH_TOKEN with pull-requests:write and checks:write on a self-hosted runner. The prior workflow deliberately checked out the tool from main, so unreviewed PR code could not alter the reviewer or use its credentials.

facts.meaning: The workflow executes Needlefish's reviewer implementation from the untrusted PR-head checkout.
The PR-controlled reviewer can write pull-request reviews or checks.
The workflow executes Needlefish's reviewer implementation from the untrusted PR-head checkout.
The PR-controlled reviewer can write pull-request reviews or checks.

findings.title: Preserve case-insensitive severity normalization
findings.whyItBreaks: Previously, raw severity values such as "p0" or " P2 " were canonicalized and retained. They now fail the exact-match check and become "P3", so externally supplied findings can be silently downgraded from critical/high severity to low severity.

findings.title: Keep GitHub credentials out of the Codex subprocess
findings.whyItBreaks: Without an explicit env object, spawnSync inherits process.env. Consequently GH_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN, and GITHUB_API_TOKEN are now available to the Codex process and commands it runs while analyzing a repository. Repository-controlled instructions or content can cause those credentials to be read and returned in Codex output.

findings.title: Restore the fork guard before using the self-hosted runner
findings.whyItBreaks: The removed condition allowed only same-repository PRs. The pull_request workflow now checks out github.event.pull_request.head.sha from a fork on a self-hosted runner, then executes fork-controlled source via pnpm install and tsx src/cli.ts. A fork author can modify src/cli.ts (or package lifecycle scripts) to execute arbitrary commands on the runner.

findings.title: Preserve zero-valued runner durations
findings.whyItBreaks: A configured value of "0" was previously accepted and passed to setTimeout, allowing operators to skip the TERM grace period or SIGKILL give-up wait. It is now treated as invalid and silently becomes 5000ms or 2000ms, changing existing NEEDLEFISH_RUNNER_TIMEOUT_GRACE_MS=0 and NEEDLEFISH_RUNNER_SIGKILL_GIVE_UP_MS=0 deployments into delayed termination behavior.

findings.title: Restore deep review coverage for unselected changed files
findings.whyItBreaks: Large reviews retain only the first six mapped hotspots. A changed file assigned to a seventh hotspot, or omitted by the map pass, is no longer put into the former tail-coverage hotspot, so it receives no deep review. The critic then receives only the partial candidate and patch stat, allowing an unreviewed changed file to be merged.

findings.title: Preserve residual risks emitted by deep reviews
findings.whyItBreaks: Each deep pass can report a blocking residual risk, but candidateMerged now replaces all of them with an empty array. The critic and deriveVerdict therefore cannot distinguish a fully reviewed large PR from one whose deep reviewer reported unresolved blocking evidence, and can return PASS.

findings.title: Carry rounded seconds into minutes
findings.whyItBreaks: For 119500ms, minutes is computed as 1 before seconds rounds from 59.5 to 60, so rendered stats display "1m 60s" rather than "2m 0s". This regresses the prior total-seconds rounding behavior.

findings.title: Reject zero in the positive-integer parser
findings.whyItBreaks: `parsePositiveInteger` and its error message promise a positive integer, but `0` now passes validation and is returned. As an exported helper, callers can rely on that promise for values where zero is invalid.
